seo.title: GEO for Restaurants: Get Picked by AI Recommendations
seo.meta_description: GEO for restaurants: how diners ask ChatGPT and Google AI where to eat, the menu, listing and review signals that matter, and quick wins for owners.

h1: GEO for Restaurants: How to Get Recommended When Diners Ask AI
answer: GEO for restaurants means making your restaurant easy for AI tools like Google AI Mode, ChatGPT and Gemini to recommend when people ask where to eat. The essentials are an up-to-date text menu, accurate hours and location, clear descriptions of cuisine, dietary options and atmosphere, consistent listings, and plenty of recent, genuine reviews.
key_takeaways: Diners now ask AI for specific recommendations, not just "restaurants near me".
A text menu on your site is essential; PDFs and images are harder to read.
Hours and details must match across every listing.
Describe dietary options, atmosphere and occasions in words.

sections.heading: How diners ask AI where to eat
sections.body_html: Restaurant searches have become conversational: "quiet Italian place in Costa Mesa for an anniversary", "kid-friendly brunch with outdoor seating near Huntington Beach", "best vegan tacos open late". AI tools answer by combining listings, reviews, menus and websites. A restaurant that clearly states what it offers, for which occasions and diets, gives the AI the details it needs to match those specific requests.

sections.heading: Put your menu in text
sections.body_html: Many restaurant sites show menus only as PDFs or photos. Those are harder for crawlers to read reliably. Publish your menu as text on a web page, with dish names, short descriptions, prices and dietary labels such as vegetarian, vegan or gluten-free. Schema.org has a Menu type, and the Restaurant type can describe cuisine, price range and opening hours. Update the page whenever the menu changes.

sections.heading: Describe the experience in words
sections.body_html:
• Atmosphere: quiet, lively, family-friendly, romantic, sports on TV.
  • Occasions: date night, groups, business lunch, celebrations.
  • Practicalities: parking, reservations, outdoor seating, accessibility, private dining.
  • Dietary options: what you can and cannot accommodate.

These are the details diners include in their questions. If they are only implied by photos, an AI may not connect your restaurant to the request.

sections.heading: Keep listings accurate
sections.body_html: Wrong hours are the fastest way to lose a diner's trust. Keep hours, holiday closures, address, phone and booking links identical across your website, Google Business Profile, Bing Places, review sites and delivery and reservation platforms. Update special hours before every holiday.

sections.heading: Reviews and recency
sections.body_html: Recommendations lean heavily on what diners say. Encourage reviews with a simple card or receipt message, reply to reviews professionally, and address recurring complaints in the restaurant, not just in replies. Reviews that mention specific dishes and occasions add useful detail. Never buy reviews or reward only positive ones.

sections.heading: Get mentioned locally
sections.body_html: Local food writers, neighborhood guides, event listings and community groups are part of what AI tools read. Host events, take part in local food festivals, and make it easy for writers to get your menu, photos and story. A mention in a respected local guide can carry into AI recommendations.

sections.heading: Quick wins this week
sections.body_html:
1. Publish a text menu page with prices and dietary labels.
  2. Check hours and holiday hours on every listing.
  3. Add an About section describing atmosphere, occasions and practicalities.
  4. Reply to your last 20 reviews.
  5. Ask Gemini, ChatGPT and Google AI Mode for restaurants like yours nearby and note who appears.

sections.heading: How to measure results
sections.body_html: Track reservations, direct orders and calls by source, visits from AI platforms in analytics, and searches for your restaurant's name. Check AI recommendations for your cuisine and neighborhood monthly. Full tables on a Tuesday are the real measure.

sections.heading: Common mistakes restaurants make
sections.body_html: The most frequent problems are holiday hours that never get updated, a website that only shows an image of the menu, different phone numbers on different platforms, and an About page with a story but no practical details. Another is ignoring reviews; unanswered complaints shape both diner decisions and the overall picture AI tools form.

sections.heading: An example About section that helps AI
sections.body_html: Instead of "a warm and inviting place for great food", try: "A 40-seat neighborhood trattoria in Costa Mesa serving handmade pasta and wood-fired dishes. Quiet enough for conversation, popular for date nights and small celebrations. Patio seating for 12, free lot parking behind the building, reservations recommended Friday and Saturday. Vegetarian dishes on every section of the menu; gluten-free pasta available." Every sentence answers something a diner might ask.

sections.heading: Delivery and ordering platforms
sections.body_html: Third-party delivery and reservation platforms are also sources AI tools may read. Keep menus, prices and hours aligned there too, and make sure your own website links to your preferred ordering and booking options.

sections.heading: Where to get help
sections.body_html: A GEO audit for a restaurant asks AI tools for places like yours in your neighborhood, for the occasions and diets you serve, and notes who appears. It checks menu readability, hours on every platform, review activity and your About details, then lists the quick fixes that matter most. Most can be done in a week.

faqs.a: It is making your restaurant easy for AI tools like Google AI Mode, ChatGPT and Gemini to recommend when people ask where to eat.

faqs.q: Do AI tools read restaurant menus?
faqs.a: They can read menus published as text on web pages more reliably than menus in PDFs or images. Include dish names, descriptions, prices and dietary labels.

faqs.q: What schema should a restaurant use?
faqs.a: Schema.org's Restaurant type can describe cuisine, price range, hours and location, and the Menu type can describe your menu.

faqs.q: How do reviews affect AI restaurant recommendations?
faqs.a: Reviews are a major input. Recent, specific reviews that mention dishes and occasions give AI tools useful detail about what you are good for.

faqs.q: Should I list dietary options on my website?
faqs.a: Yes. Diners often ask for vegan, vegetarian or gluten-free options, so stating clearly what you offer helps match those requests.

faqs.q: How quickly can a restaurant improve AI recommendations?
faqs.a: Fixing listings and publishing a text menu can help within weeks. Building review volume and local mentions takes longer.

faqs.q: Does my restaurant need its own website if I am on delivery apps?
faqs.a: Yes. Your own site is where you control the menu, story and details. Delivery platforms are useful but do not replace a clear, accurate website.

faqs.q: Do photos help AI restaurant recommendations?
faqs.a: Photos help diners decide, but AI tools rely mainly on text. Pair photos with written descriptions of dishes, atmosphere and amenities.

faqs.q: Should I respond to negative reviews?
faqs.a: Yes, calmly and specifically. A professional reply shows you take feedback seriously, and fixing recurring issues improves future reviews.
